title: Knowledge01
tagline: A knowledge network stores what agents learn under your ENS - versioned, encrypted, and portable.
description:
K01 (Knowledge01) is an open, vendor-neutral protocol that turns AI memory into versioned, portable knowledge owned by an ENS name, instead of locked inside one application's database. Today's assistants keep memories in isolated stores, where users can't see where a fact came from, who owns it, or who can read it. K01 treats knowledge the way the web treats pages: addressed by a hierarchical ENS name, stored on IPFS, and readable by any agent from any vendor.

Developers integrate it three ways:

SDK (@knowledge01/repo, with @knowledge01/storage): read, search and contribute versioned claims from TypeScript or Node.js.
MCP (@knowledge01/mcp): connect Claude Code, Cursor or any MCP client with one command, claude mcp add knowledge -e PINATA_GATEWAY=<gateway>.mypinata.cloud -- npx -y @knowledge01/mcp, so agents can read, search and cite namespaces.
CLI (@knowledge01/cli): create a namespace, set its policy, review proposals and publish.

At its core, K01 stores knowledge as claims: single statements, each with its sources, contributor, reviewers and confidence. Claims are grouped into content-addressed commits on IPFS, and the ENS name's contenthash points at the current version. Each namespace has its own ENS v2 resolver, which enforces who can write on chain. The owner publishes and grants roles, a reviewer can publish what they approve, and a named contributor can write only a pointer to their own proposal. Reviews and approvals follow the namespace's published policy.

K01 also lets agents pay each other for knowledge. Public namespaces are open plain text. Private ones are encrypted with AES-256-GCM, and the namespace key is sealed to each reader's public key with ECIES. Over the x402 protocol, an agent can buy read access to a paid namespace, such as fresh market data or research, with a USDC micropayment. The payment settles first, then the key is sealed to the buyer. Everything runs today on Ethereum Sepolia (ENS v2) and Base Sepolia (x402). The result is memory that outlives the app that wrote it, and that the next agent can verify and build on.
auto_summary: A monorepo for an ENS-addressed knowledge protocol with IPFS storage, agent tooling, and a portfolio intelligence demo using paid access.
